props.title: Battleship
props.initialSlug: Navy vs. alien warships in ocean warfare epic

sections.content: **Battleship (2012)** (2012) represents peak Hollywood hubris - a $220 million attempt to turn a Hasbro board game into the next **Transformers** (2007). Director Peter Berg delivers bombastic naval warfare and alien invasion spectacle, but the film epitomizes the early 2010s trend of forcing recognizable brands into generic action blockbusters. Like **G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra** (2009) and **John Carter** (2012), it prioritizes CGI destruction over coherent storytelling, though Taylor Kitsch and Rihanna's performances add some charm to the proceedings.

sections.content: The film's failure highlighted Hollywood's misguided obsession with pre-existing IP. While **Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl** (2003) successfully adapted a theme park ride through creative world-building, **Battleship** (2012) merely grafts alien invaders onto naval warfare imagery. The forced "peg" targeting system reference feels particularly strained. Compare this to **Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World** (2003), which creates authentic naval drama through attention to historical detail and character development.

Despite its flaws, **Battleship** (2012) features impressive naval combat choreography and effects work. The destruction sequences rival **Pearl Harbor** (2001) and Midway (2019) in scale, even if the narrative lacks their historical weight. Berg's direction shines in the action beats, suggesting the potential for a more grounded naval thriller in the vein of The Hunt for Red October (1990) or **Crimson Tide** (1995). movies.title: U-571
movies.slug: WWII submarine crew attempts to capture an Enigma machine from the Germans

sections.content: **Battleship** (2012) marked a turning point for naval warfare films, as subsequent releases like **Captain Phillips** (2013) and **Greyhound** (2020) returned to reality-based scenarios over sci-fi spectacle. The genre has historically succeeded with authentic stories, from **Das Boot** (1981) to **Black Sea** (2014), suggesting audiences prefer naval tension grounded in plausible scenarios rather than alien invasion fantasies.
